title: Book: Your Money or Your Life — Vicki Robin and Joe Dominguez (1992)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: This book reframes money as 'life energy': the hours of your life you trade for it. Its method has you track every rupee, work out your real hourly wage by subtracting the costs of working (commuting, work clothes, stress spending) from your pay, and ask for each purchase whether it is worth the life energy it costs and whether it brings fulfilment. Over time you aim for 'enough' and the 'crossover point', where income from your investments covers your expenses, giving financial independence. The idea of converting prices into hours of work also appears in this app's work-hours cost view. Cautions: the 'live on investment income' target depends on assumptions about returns and withdrawals that are unsettled, and its frugal lifestyle may not suit everyone — borrow the awareness, not necessarily the extremes.
